knowledge_graph.title: World Mental Health Day
knowledge_graph.description: World Mental Health Day is an international day for global mental health education, awareness and advocacy against social stigma. It was first celebrated in 1992 at the initiative of the World Federation for Mental Health, a global mental health organization with members and contacts in more than 150 countries.

related_questions.question: Is it okay to take a mental health day from work?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is generally okay to take a mental health day from work. It's a valid form of self-care and can be beneficial for your overall well-being, just like taking a sick day for a physical illness. Many workplaces recognize mental health as a valid reason for taking time off to rest and recharge.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, it is generally okay to take a mental health day from work

text_blocks.snippet: Why take a mental health day?

list.snippet: Burnout prevention: A mental health day can help prevent burnout and reduce stress levels.
Improved mental well-being: It allows you to focus on your mental health, de-stress, and recharge.
Increased productivity: By taking time to address your mental health, you can return to work feeling more focused and productive.
Better work-life balance: It helps maintain a healthy balance between work and personal life.

text_blocks.snippet: When to consider a mental health day:

list.snippet: When you're experiencing increased stress, anxiety, or burnout.
When you're having difficulty focusing or concentrating at work.
When your mental health symptoms are interfering with your ability to function effectively.
When you feel emotionally drained or overwhelmed.

text_blocks.snippet: How to approach taking a mental health day:

list.title: Check your workplace policy:
list.snippet: See if your company has a policy regarding mental health days.

list.title: Communicate with your manager:
list.snippet: Inform your manager that you need to take a day off for mental health reasons, similar to how you would for a physical illness.

list.title: Use your sick leave:
list.snippet: In many cases, mental health days can be taken under your existing sick leave policy.

list.title: Don't be afraid to advocate for your needs:
list.snippet: Prioritizing your mental health is important, and it's okay to take the time you need to care for yourself.

text_blocks.snippet: In California, employees can use accrued paid sick leave for mental health reasons, including attending therapy or counseling sessions or taking a day to recover from stress or burnout.
In conclusion, taking a mental health day is a healthy and acceptable practice, and it's important to prioritize your well-being.

related_questions.question: What to say when you need a mental health day?

text_blocks.snippet: When requesting a mental health day, you can keep it simple and professional by stating you need a sick day for personal health reasons or to focus on your well-being. You don't need to disclose specific details about your mental health if you're not comfortable, but you can mention that you're feeling overwhelmed or need to recharge. Providing a plan for work coverage can also ease concerns about your absence.
snippet_highlighted_words: you need a sick day for personal health reasons or to focus on your well-being

text_blocks.snippet: Here are a few options for what to say:

list.snippet: "I'm not feeling well and need to take a sick day today. I'll be back tomorrow."
"I'm feeling unwell and need to take a day to rest."
"I'm taking a mental health day to focus on my well-being."
"I'm feeling burnt out and need to take a mental health day to recharge. I'll be back tomorrow."
"I'm experiencing some personal health issues and need to take a sick day."
"I'm having a hard time with my mental health and need to take a sick day today. Thank you for your understanding."
"I've been feeling overwhelmed lately and need to take a mental health day to focus on my well-being. I've ensured my current projects are on track and will check in if anything urgent arises."
"I'm struggling with my mental health and would like to take a sick day to focus on my well-being. I'll be back tomorrow, and I've made sure that [colleague's name] is aware of my current projects."
"I need to take a day to focus on my mental health. I'll be sure to check in on emails periodically, but I'll be taking the day to recharge."
Be honest: While you don't need to overshare, being truthful about your need for a day off is important.
Keep it professional: Use clear and direct language.
Offer work coverage: If you can, provide a plan for how your work will be handled in your absence.
Respect your privacy: You don't have to disclose more than you're comfortable with.
Consider company culture: If your workplace is supportive of mental health, you may feel more comfortable being open about your need for a mental health day.
Focus on self-care: Once you've requested the day off, use the time to relax, recharge, and focus on your well-being.
